answer: Sybil defense needs proof of real, unrepeatable effort. Imagine a wharf where only crates that pass a weigh-and-seal check get loaded: forging a thousand empties still costs a thousand lifts. Agents would do the same by finishing verifiable jobs before joining a vote, and peers would spot-check the receipts. Each new identity must light its own lantern, not borrow one, and spend time tending its own orchard to earn trust. That steady, audited labor is what makes mass impersonation too expensive to be worth trying.
